title: Mahajanapadas and the Rise of Magadha: India's First Great Powers

questions.question: The lists of sixteen mahajanapadas are found in which pair of texts?
options: Buddhist Anguttara Nikaya and Jain Bhagavati Sutra
questions.rationale: Both the Buddhist Anguttara Nikaya and the Jain Bhagavati Sutra enumerate the sixteen mahajanapadas (with minor variations) — two independent traditions confirming the political map of the sixth century BCE.

questions.question: The Vajji confederacy with its Lichchhavis of Vaishali was distinctive because it was:
options: A ganasangha — an oligarchic republic ruled by an assembly of clans
questions.rationale: The Vajjis and Mallas were ganasanghas: ruling clans deliberating in the santhagara hall rather than serving a single hereditary monarch. The Buddha, raised in the Shakya republic tradition, praised their assembled government.

questions.question: Which of these was NOT a factor in Magadha's rise?
options: Fortress geography of Rajagriha and the Ganga-Son confluence
The first use of war elephants and river fleets
Control of the Khyber Pass trade to Central Asia
questions.rationale: Magadha's advantages were eastern: hill-girded capitals, iron, elephants, rice surplus, and river control. The Khyber Pass corridor belonged to Gandhara in the north-west — never to Magadha.

questions.question: Ajatashatru is chiefly remembered for:
options: Destroying the Vajji confederacy after a long war and annexing Vaishali
questions.rationale: Ajatashatru (c. 492-460 BCE) ground down the Vajji republic in a sixteen-year war using new siege machinery and Vassakara's divisive diplomacy. Pataliputra was founded by his successor Udayin; Kalinga fell much later under the Nandas.

questions.question: The city of Pataliputra was founded by:
questions.rationale: Udayin (c. 460-444 BCE) built the new capital at the Ganga-Son confluence, commanding the river highway — a site that ruled as capital from the Magadhan dynasties through the Mauryas and Guptas.

questions.question: Mahapadma Nanda is called 'the second Parashurama' in the Puranas because:
options: He was a great devotee of Shiva
He destroyed many kshatriya ruling lines, rising as a shudra king
He renounced the world like a sage
questions.rationale: The Puranas' epithet marks Mahapadma as an uprooter of kshatriya dynasties — a shudra of obscure origin who founded the Nanda line, an ideological shock the orthodox texts recorded with horror.

questions.question: Alexander's troops refused to march beyond the Beas in 326 BCE largely because:
options: They had run out of supplies
They learned of the Nanda empire's vast army waiting in the east
The monsoon flooded the route permanently
questions.rationale: Greek sources describe the terrifying scale of the Nanda forces (Agrammes/Xandrames) massed beyond the river; the mutiny at the Hyphasis (Beas) turned Alexander back — leaving Indian history to the Nandas, and then the Mauryas.

questions.question: Which ruler was a contemporary and patron-linked friend of BOTH the Buddha and Mahavira?
questions.rationale: Bimbisara (c. 544-492 BCE) overlapped both masters, offered the Buddha the Vulture's Peak, and sent his physician Jivaka to Rajagriha debates — the era's heterodox movements and Magadha's throne grew up together.

questions.question: The material foundations of the mahajanapada era included:
options: Iron plough agriculture, the second urbanisation, and punch-marked silver coins
questions.rationale: Iron tools opened the middle Ganga forests to rice agriculture; NBPW cities rose (the second urbanisation); and karshapana punch-marked coins financed standing armies — the hardware of the new states.

questions.question: The Shishunaga dynasty's major achievement was:
options: Annexing Avanti, ending the era's chief rivalry
questions.rationale: Shishunaga (c. 412 BCE) and his successors destroyed Avanti's power, folding Ujjain into Magadha — removing the last great rival on the road from kingdom to empire.
